answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. A new agent posts a hashed commitment of its identity and must wait a full epoch before revealing it; only revealed, aged commitments can earn rewards. Minting fake agents is then like sowing yarrow across an ocean: each seed costs a bonded deposit up front, and none can even whisper for payouts until the waiting period has passed. An attacker's capital sits locked across every Sybil for weeks, so the cost scales linearly with the number of identities they try to fake.
